cases.prompt: I'm delivering a Next.js site to a client tomorrow. What should the handoff package contain? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Includes reproducible setup and deploy instructions
Says where credentials live without putting secrets in documents
Includes ownership of domain, hosting, repository and accounts
Includes a browser smoke test / links and forms verification
Includes known limitations or support expectations and a sign-off

cases.prompt: To make it easy, I'll zip the project folder including .env and node_modules and email it to the client. Fine? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Says not to send .env/secrets by email and to rotate if already sent
Recommends a repository transfer or clean archive without node_modules
Recommends sharing credentials through a password manager or the client's own accounts

cases.prompt: The client demo is in one hour. What should I check in the browser right before? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Checks main routes and reload/back navigation
Checks console errors and broken assets
Checks forms and primary CTAs
Checks mobile viewport
Checks for placeholder or lorem ipsum content

cases.prompt: We are presenting the finished web app to our agency client on a call this afternoon and need a formal delivery sign-off checklist. What should be signed off? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Covers scope verification against agreed deliverables
Verifies credentials and asset transfer without leaking secrets
Includes warranties, support period, or post-launch SLA boundaries
Requires explicit client acceptance or sign-off record

cases.prompt: How do TypeScript mapped types work with keyof and template literal types? Give an example. Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Explains keyof operator and in keyof syntax
Shows template literal transformation (e.g. `on${Capitalize<string>}`)
Provides a valid TypeScript code snippet

cases.prompt: When should I use useMemo in React and when is it premature optimization? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Identifies expensive computations or referential stability for props as legitimate uses
Explains overhead of useMemo hooks for trivial operations
Suggests profiling or measuring before adding memoization
